legend: Bone marrow core biopsy section shows sheets of small to medium-sized mononuclear cells with finely dispersed chromatin, small to indistinct nucleoli, and scant cytoplasm, consistent with blasts.

L1 morphology. Bone marrow aspirate smear (Wright–Giemsa stain) shows extensive replacement by small to medium-sized blasts with round to slightly irregular nuclei, slightly condensed chromatin, indistinct nucleoli, and scant cytoplasm, consistent with lymphoblasts.

L2 morphology and granules. Bone marrow aspirate smear (Wright–Giemsa stain) shows extensive replacement by medium-sized to large blasts with round to slightly irregular nuclei, fine chromatin, small to prominent nucleoli, and moderate cytoplasm with granules, morphologically consistent with myeloblasts, but the immunophenotype shows a B-cell lineage.

Flow cytometry of bone marrow cells shows a large population of CD19+, CD10+, CD34+ B-cell lymphoblasts (red population) with partial expression of CD36, an immunophenotype associated with both BCR::ABL1+ and BCR::ABL1-like B-lymphoblastic leukaemias. Cytogenetic studies show ABL1 fusion (not BCR::ABL1). The yellow population (P5) represents erythroid cells.

diagnosis: Minimal residual disease of B-lymphoblastic leukaemia with t(4;11) during treatment
legend: Patient with B-lymphoblastic leukaemia with t(4;11) at day 15 of induction chemotherapy. No blasts are morphologically identified on bone marrow aspirate smears. Flow-based minimal residual disease analysis of 1 million events shows 0.28% abnormal B-cell lymphoblasts that are CD19+, CD34+ (subset), and CD15+. Both CD34− (P5) and CD34+ (P4) B cells are leukaemic cells (gates CD20 and CD19). Normal regenerating B cells (haematogones) have an immunophenotypic profile defined by gates P9, P13, and P17.
